html:
The Nobel Prizes have been given since 1901 under the will of the Swedish inventor and industrialist Alfred Nobel, who made his fortune from dynamite. They are the best known awards in the world.

Nobel died in 1896 and left most of his money for prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature and peace. Swedish bodies choose the first four, and a committee of the Norwegian parliament chooses the Peace Prize, awarded in Oslo. A prize in economics was added by the Swedish central bank in 1968.

The prizes are handed out each 10 December, the day of Nobel's death. They have rewarded discoveries from radioactivity to the structure of DNA, and made Sweden a referee of world science and culture. Choices for the literature and peace prizes are often debated.
